anatomy.intro: White radial spines and wool form a pale coat around the longer brown central hooks.

parts.function: Fine covering between the tubercles helps create the silky appearance.
parts.label: White wool

parts.function: Pale spreading spokes surround each spine-bearing areole.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: A stronger reddish-brown hook projects through the white covering.
parts.label: Hooked central spine

parts.function: A young side head can develop into another cylinder within the clump.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: Deep rose-pink flowers about 1.5 cm across form near the crown. As in other Mammillaria, they emerge between tubercles, separate from the spine clusters.

growth.note: Heads lengthen into short cylinders as basal offsets build a mound around them.

stages.text: A living juvenile begins as a small spiny globe.
stages.title: Young head

stages.text: The stem lengthens and develops a dense pale coat.
stages.title: Longer cylinder

stages.text: Offsets can gather into a spreading group.
stages.title: Cluster of heads

habitat.text: Mammillaria bombycina is native to southwestern Aguascalientes and northeastern Jalisco, Mexico, where it grows in dry shrubland.

lookalikes.name: Mammillaria cf. rekoi
lookalikes.text: Both may have hooked central spines; the rekoi candidate has more exposed green tissue and a less heavily woolled appearance.

mature.text: Living plants develop clustered cylindrical stems about 20 cm tall, with offsets gradually widening the mound.

milestones.text: Final inspection found only a tiny surviving green patch; no offset was retained. The page preserves the plant's history.
milestones.title: Removed from the collection
